perf.summary: Hoist the loop-invariant float3 splats (processNoise*dt and measurementNoise) out of the per-iteration path.
perf.currentCost: Inside the loop each iteration constructs 'new float3(processNoise * dt)' in PredictCovariance and 'new float3(measurementNoise)' plus 'new float3(1.0f)' in Update. processNoise, dt, measurementNoise are loop-invariant, so these splats and the processNoise*dt multiply are recomputed every iteration.
perf.proposedChange: Precompute before the loop: float3 covInc = new float3(processNoise * dt); float3 measNoise = new float3(measurementNoise); float3 one = new float3(1.0f); and pass/use them inside. Or inline the math in Run using these hoisted vectors.
perf.rationale: Removes a scalar multiply plus several scalar->float3 broadcast constructions from each iteration. On SIMD the splat is cheap but still an instruction; hoisting shortens the body and frees the scheduler. Burst may hoist automatically, but making it explicit guarantees it.
perf.risk: None; values are loop-invariant and identical, results bit-for-bit unchanged. Only consideration is whether to change the helper signatures (API break) versus inlining in Run.

perf.summary: Peel first iteration to drop the per-iteration 'if (i > 0)' branch and the redundant outStates[i-1] vector load.
perf.currentCost: Each iteration evaluates 'if (i > 0)' and, when true, reloads the float3 outStates[i-1] (12 bytes) from memory though it equals the previous iteration's 'state' held in registers.
perf.proposedChange: Handle i==0 before the loop (no velocity update), keep a 'float3 prev = state' register, then loop i=1..count computing velocity = (state - prev) / dt; prev = state; outStates[i] = state. Removes the branch and the memory reload.
perf.rationale: Eliminates count branch checks and count-1 float3 loads, and turns the velocity update into a register-only op, shortening the dependency chain and improving SIMD scheduling.
perf.risk: Add an explicit 'if (count <= 0) return;' guard before the peeled prologue. Outputs are identical since outStates[i-1] always equals the prior state.

perf.currentCost: 'using System;' is imported but nothing from System is referenced (only Unity.Mathematics.float3 and MethodImpl).
perf.rationale: Dead import; trivial clarity cleanup with zero runtime effect.
